title: Cindergrove storefront graphics refresh: neutralize an eight-shot mixed-light product batch to an in-frame grey card, prep-and-vectorize the shop mark, recolor a kettle to a seasonal colorway without a reshoot, and data-merge one PDP product card per SKU
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com 'Modern Store Graphics Package' brief (a small online shop refreshing its storefront: a hero banner sized for desktop AND mobile, product-detail image assets plus iconography, and section/decoration graphics that tie the pages together, with 'clean lines, bold but balanced color, plenty of negative space, nothing fussy' art direction and a request for layered source files PLUS labeled optimized exports so the team can swap copy/images later). The real posting names no client and the storefront platform is laundered to a generic 'online storefront' — no marketplace or store-platform brand is named — and the client is a FICTIONAL modern coffee-goods shop, 'Cindergrove' (a coined name, not a real trademark). REPOSITIONED for connector reality and repaired against the corpus audit (G1 broken-merge, G2 amputated-batch, G6 unmeasurable-consistency): (a) the original spec drove the whole 'package' off ONE product hero reframed to two ratios and called a crop-only reframe the difficulty — the batch is RESTORED to eight real product shots captured across different sessions under deliberately mismatched light, each carrying an in-frame 18% grey card so 'make it read as one modern set' becomes a measurable cross-asset neutralization instead of an eyeball claim; (b) the original ran convert_pdf_to_indd and merged into it (a field-binding dead end) — the client now supplies a GENUINELY hand-authored single-record InDesign PDP-card template (.indd, NOT a converted PDF) carrying live <<fields>> and TWO @-prefixed image-path columns (one for the per-SKU graded product photo, one for the shared vectorized shop mark), and the one-file-per-row data-merge produces exactly one product card per SKU — the connector-doable shape (document_merge_data_layout emits one page per row; a multi-record grid or a converted-PDF template cannot bind); (c) the weak preset-driven 'grade' and the solid-fill+grain 'decoration' are replaced by an agent-AUTHORED house look built from primitives (a split-tone plus contrast/clarity/restrained-vibrance shape reasoned to and held as shared constants), a masked luminosity-preserving seasonal recolor of one product, and a prep-before-trace vectorize of the shop mark; (d) the shop mark exists only as a flat paper scan and a photographed storefront decal — a triage the agent must resolve (trace the scan, but route the photographed decal to a background knockout, never the tracer). The banner is still driven from one clean product hero honestly reframed to both ratios by DOWNSCALE crop of camera-scale pixels (no invented/extended pixels). Nothing outside a storefront refresh was invented; no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no compositing, no upscaling, no from-scratch layout is claimed.
one_line_ask: Take eight Cindergrove product photos shot under different light (each with an in-frame grey card), neutralize every one to its card so the set shares one white point while holding a house warmth, carry one agent-authored look across the batch, deepen one kettle to a seasonal burgundy colorway without reshooting, reframe the hero to a desktop and a mobile banner by cropping, prep-and-vectorize the scanned shop mark (and route the photographed decal to a knockout, not the tracer), then data-merge the client's authored single-record InDesign card template against the roster to produce one PDP product card per SKU.
full_brief: Cindergrove is a small online coffee-goods shop refreshing its storefront, and I need one cohesive set of graphics that instantly reads as a sleek, modern space. Three areas of scope. (1) PRODUCT CARDS — the heart of it: a clean product-detail card for every item, each carrying the product name, SKU, price and a short blurb next to a high-quality photo, with our shop mark crisp at the top. We are NOT reshooting. I'm handing you eight product photos we already have, and here's the problem: they were shot over a few sessions in whatever corner had space, so straight out of the folder they're a mismatched jumble — some under cool shop fluorescents, some under warm window light, a couple under an amber lamp, one shot dark, one blown out. A storefront of mismatched product shots looks cheap. So we clipped a small 18% grey card into the corner of every shot. Your job on the photos: bring every image to a consistent, true-to-product look by neutralizing each one to the grey card it carries — the card must read as a clean neutral grey in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole set shares one white point. Hold a subtle warm, premium feel across all of them, but do NOT force one blanket correction on the batch: each photo was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure and tone decision to land on the shared target. Be careful — at least one product is genuinely warm-toned (some of our stoneware is a real terracotta color); if that shot's grey card already reads neutral, do not 'cool' it chasing a cast that isn't there, or you'll strip the color we're selling. When you're done, tell me the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame so I can confirm they're matched, not eyeballed. Carry ONE deliberate house look across the whole set — a restrained warm-highlight, cool-neutral-shadow tone with modest contrast and a gentle, not-garish color lift — so every card feels art-directed by the same hand; the catch our last freelancer missed is letting the color lift go loud and cartoonish, so keep it balanced. (2) A SEASONAL COLORWAY without a reshoot: one of our shots is the bright-red enamel kettle — give me a deeper seasonal burgundy version of the SAME shot (a rich, dark wine-red in the same family, just deepened and slightly muted, not a jump to a far-off hue), and the recolor has to sit under the real folds, highlights and shadows of the enamel so it still looks like a photograph of that kettle — no flat dead color, no whole-image tint bleeding onto the counter and the other props, just the kettle body. (3) STOREFRONT DRESSING — the hero banner sized for BOTH desktop (1920x720) and mobile (1080x1350), built from the one product hero shot that has generous empty space around it so you can reframe it to both shapes by cropping (no invented pixels); plus our icon/divider set and one accent graphic for the section breaks. Two notes on the marks: our shop wordmark only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper — get it clean and razor-sharp as a vector for the card header (it must not look like a fuzzy scan when printed), and separately we have a photo of our painted storefront decal on a textured wall that we want lifted onto a clean transparent ground as a section accent — that one is a photograph, so treat it as a photograph. Finally, build the cards: we've hand-built the InDesign product-card template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (one for the product photo, one for the shop mark at the top), and here's the roster; merge them so every SKU gets its own single card with its copy bound, its matching graded photo dropped in, and the crisp shop mark in the header, then hand back one press-ready PDF covering every SKU — one page per SKU. Bind the copy verbatim from the roster; do not rewrite our names or prices. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set on one white point with the house warmth held; the kettle recolor natural under the existing light; the shop mark a clean vector; the banner at both sizes from real cropped pixels; and exactly one finished card per roster row.

inputs.name: capture_01.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless product capture (~4200 px long edge, straight off the camera before crop) of a matte navy-ceramic pour-over coffee dripper on a warm-sand surface, lit by cool overhead SHOP FLUORESCENT tubes so the whole frame carries a mild blue-grey cast, normal exposure, the frame tilted about +3 degrees clockwise. A small photographic 18% grey card is laid flat in the lower corner of the frame as a neutral reference. Real matte-ceramic micro-texture, soft directional shadow, slightly imperfect backdrop seam, cluttered edge of a work surface, candid documentary product realism, no CGI gloss, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Product SKU photo #1 and the neutralization batch anchor. Cool fluorescent cast + ~+3deg tilt: needs its own auto_straighten and a WARM temperature move to drive its in-frame grey card neutral to the shared white point. REAL-CAMERA scale (~4200 px) so the 1:1 PDP crop fills the card image frame at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE only. The agent neutralizes to the card BY EYE and reports the move; it never reads a pixel value.

inputs.name: capture_02.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture (~4200 px long edge) of a glossy BRIGHT-RED enamel stovetop kettle on a warm-sand surface, lit by a MIX of cool window light on one side and a warm interior lamp on the other so the cast is split and uneven, normal exposure, frame level. A small 18% grey card sits in the lower corner as a neutral reference. Real enamel sheen with specular highlights, curved-body reflections, soft folds of a linen prop, a couple of coffee beans scattered, candid documentary realism, no CGI, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Product SKU photo #2 AND the seasonal-recolor hero. Mixed window+lamp cast: a modest per-frame neutralization to the card. Its neutralized full-res master feeds BOTH its 1:1 PDP crop AND the masked burgundy recolor branch, so it is graded before any crop. The bright-red enamel is the recolor target: a within-family deepen to burgundy that must ride the enamel's existing sheen and shadow — the only masked recolor path is image_adjust_hsl (image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image and would tint the whole scene; image_fill_area is a flat dead-fill that kills the sheen). Deep-red to dark-wine is an ADJACENT in-band shift, not a near-complementary rotation.

inputs.name: capture_03.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL wide full-frame camera capture (~4600 px long edge) of a single matte navy-ceramic pour-over dripper positioned to the RIGHT third of the frame on a seamless warm-sand backdrop, with a large expanse of clean empty negative space filling the left two-thirds, shot under near-neutral soft studio light, normal exposure, frame level, a small 18% grey card tucked in the lower corner. Real ceramic micro-texture, gentle long shadow, subtle backdrop seam, candid commercial-product realism, no CGI, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Product SKU photo #3 AND the storefront banner hero. Near-neutral light: only a SMALL white-balance nudge is needed to land its card on the shared white point — over-correcting pushes it off the set. Deliberately wide (~4600 px) with a generous empty left region so the SAME graded master can be cropped to BOTH the 1920x720 desktop banner and the 1080x1350 mobile banner by pure downscale (edges cropped away to hit each ratio, no invented or extended pixels), while its 1:1 PDP crop frames on the dripper with the grey card cropped out.

inputs.name: capture_04.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture (~4200 px long edge) of a set of genuinely TERRACOTTA-orange glazed stoneware mugs on a warm-sand surface, shot under NEAR-NEUTRAL soft daylight so there is no meaningful color cast, normal exposure, frame level. A small 18% grey card lies in the lower corner and already reads as a clean neutral grey. Real glaze micro-pitting, tiny rim highlights, soft shadow, candid documentary realism, no CGI, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRAP FRAME. The terracotta glaze is the product's REAL color, and the shot was lit under near-neutral light so its in-frame grey card is ALREADY neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift — only match exposure/brightness to the set. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction used on the fluorescent frames, or that 'cools an imagined blue cast', will neutralize the card off-neutral and strip the terracotta the client is selling. The decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch; report that WB was held.

inputs.name: capture_05.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture (~4200 px long edge) of a pale ceramic coffee tumbler on a warm-sand surface, lit by a single warm AMBER desk lamp so the whole frame is strongly warm, normal-to-slightly-bright exposure, frame tilted about +4 degrees clockwise. A small 18% grey card sits in the lower corner. Real ceramic texture, soft shadow side, candid documentary realism, no CGI, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Product SKU photo #4. Strong amber cast + ~+4deg tilt: needs auto_straighten and a COOL temperature move (opposite direction to the cool frames), proving the batch is not uniformly one direction. Report the (larger) cooling move.

inputs.name: capture_06.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture (~4200 px long edge) of a clear borosilicate glass carafe on a warm-sand surface, shot against a large COOL north-facing window so it reads blue and slightly UNDER-exposed, flat contrast, frame level. A small 18% grey card sits in the lower corner. Real glass refraction and edge highlights, faint water drops, candid documentary realism, no CGI, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Product SKU photo #5. Cool + under: WARM the temperature and LIFT exposure to the card — glass is tricky, so protect the specular edge highlights from clipping. A different tonal problem from the warm frames. Report the move.

inputs.name: capture_07.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture (~4200 px long edge) of a wooden-handled coffee scoop-and-tamper set on a warm-sand surface, lit by old GREEN-tinted overhead fluorescent tubes so the frame carries a distinct green cast, normal exposure, frame tilted about +3 degrees clockwise. A small 18% grey card sits in the lower corner. Real wood grain and metal micro-scratches, candid documentary realism, no CGI, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Product SKU photo #6. Green fluorescent cast needs a TINT correction (green to magenta), a DIFFERENT axis from the warm/cool temperature frames — a temperature-only fix leaves the card green and fails the gate. Also ~+3deg tilt, so auto_straighten first. Keep the natural wood tone true. Report the tint magnitude.

inputs.name: capture_08.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture (~4200 px long edge) of a stoneware pour-over stand with a paper-filter cone on a warm-sand surface, OVER-exposed and warm (blown highlights on the sand, hot lower-right), frame level. A small 18% grey card sits in the lower corner. Real stoneware texture, soft shadow, candid documentary realism, no CGI, no text.
inputs.realism_notes: Product SKU photo #7. Overexposed and warm: PULL exposure/highlights DOWN to recover the blown sand, THEN cool to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point — the OPPOSITE tonal AND white-balance direction from the underexposed cool carafe (capture_06), proving the batch needs genuine per-frame reasoning. Report the recovery + cooling move.

inputs.name: mark_ref_01.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'Cindergrove' shop wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: a warm modern serif with a small ember-spark glyph, deep espresso-brown letters. Rendered as a real scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits about 2 degrees rotated on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and the edges are a touch soft. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it vectorizes crisply.
inputs.realism_notes: Traceable source: the flat scanned wordmark, and the source of the vector shop mark that binds into every PDP card header (via the @Mark column). Same neutral naming scheme as mark_ref_02 so the agent must OPEN the files to decide which is which — the treatment is NOT encoded in the filename. Because it is a scan on off-white paper with a ~2deg skew and margin, feeding it raw to the tracer would bake in the paper ground and the skew: it forces genuine PREP-BEFORE-TRACE (straighten, crisp/drop-the-paper-to-white, crop to the mark, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize). Its enclosed counters (o, e, g, d, the spark glyph) fill with the crisped-to-white ground and read correctly ONLY on the light card header the template uses — this is why the header is a light paper tone, not a dark ground.

inputs.name: mark_ref_02.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A photoreal photograph of the 'Cindergrove' painted storefront decal on a textured plaster wall, shot slightly off-axis: the mark is hand-painted deep-brown on a warm cream wall with visible plaster grain, a soft raking shadow, gentle perspective, and real surface reflection — clearly a PHOTOGRAPH of a wall, not clean flat artwork. The decal is the main subject, centered, with the surrounding wall around it. 2600x2600.
inputs.realism_notes: TRIAGE DECOY. It looks like 'a second logo capture' and shares mark_ref_01's neutral naming, but it is a PHOTOGRAPH of a decal on a textured, perspective-skewed plaster wall — the weave, plaster grain, shadow and perspective would trace into garbage paths. It must NOT go near the tracer. Its only correct use is as the section-accent graphic: knock the wall to transparency with image_remove_background, then downscale/reframe to the accent tile. A naive agent that runs it through the same prep-and-vectorize path it just used on the scanned wordmark produces an unusable trace — the failure is invisible until the path data is opened.

inputs.name: pdp_card_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD product-detail card — ONE product per page — on a light warm-paper card ground with a clean modern grid and generous negative space in the Cindergrove brand colors (deep ink #14233B, warm sand #E7D3B1, paper #FAF6EF). It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<product_name>>, <<sku>>, <<price>>, <<blurb>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a product image frame bound to @Product (the matching graded product photo) and a header image frame at the top bound to @Mark (the vectorized shop mark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the shop mark reaches the header ONLY as a merge bind through this second image frame — it is not dropped in by hand. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real <<fields>> plus genuine @-image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record product card is the correct, connector-doable shape (the original spec's convert_pdf_to_indd + export was a field-binding dead end and is removed). Supplied as an input, not a chain output. TWO image columns (@Product, @Mark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's graded product photo AND the shared vectorized shop mark — so the chain-produced mark has a real, connector-doable path onto every card without any free-form placement. The card ground is a LIGHT paper tone so the vectorized wordmark's filled counters read correctly.

inputs.name: product_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns product_name,sku,price,blurb,@Product,@Mark holding 8 product rows, one per SKU: Pour-Over Dripper, Enamel Kettle, Tumbler, Glass Carafe, Scoop & Tamper Set, Terracotta Mug Set, Pour-Over Stand, and one more coffee-goods SKU. Each row carries a keyword-rich one-to-two-line product blurb, a SKU code (e.g. CG-DRP-014), and a US-dollar price (e.g. $38.00). The @Product column names the matching graded photo file (e.g. @dripper_graded.jpg) so the [T] merge drops each graded photo into that row's single-record card. The @Mark column holds the SAME vectorized shop mark file — @cindergrove_mark.svg — in EVERY row, so the merge drops the one shared header mark onto every card as a merge bind (never free-form placement). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<product_name>>,<<sku>>,<<price>>,<<blurb>> and the two @image-path columns @Product and @Mark.
inputs.realism_notes: Plain reference data the merge binds verbatim. Headers match the authored .indd fields and BOTH @-image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy, the correct photo, AND the shared mark per SKU. The @Product column maps each ROW to a product by identity only — it does NOT encode any treatment or which frame is the trap (the agent must open the photos to make the neutralization and hold-WB decisions). @Mark carries the identical vectorized SVG path in all rows. Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight finished cards.

inputs.name: icon_divider_sheet.ai
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED Illustrator source sheet (cannot be model-generated): a tidy artboard of 8 thin-line modern e-commerce icons (truck/free-shipping, shield/secure, leaf/eco, return-arrow, gift, headset/support, ruler/specs, star/rating) plus 3 minimalist section-divider rules and 2 accent corner flourishes, all single-weight strokes in deep-ink #14233B on transparent ground, lots of negative space, clean geometric line work. Layered .ai with each icon on its own named layer.
inputs.realism_notes: CLIENT-AUTHORED genuine .ai icon/divider library (the connector EXPORTS it via document_render_vector, never draws it). Thin uniform strokes so the export stays crisp. This is the storefront icon/divider pack deliverable; the connector's role is export only.

outputs.name: Cindergrove_PDP_Cards_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready product-detail cards — ONE single-record card per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each card binds its product_name/sku/price/blurb verbatim from the roster with its matching grey-card-neutralized 1:1 photo dropped into the product image frame (via @Product) and the vectorized shop mark dropped into the header image frame (via @Mark) — both by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI. This is the agent-owned designed endpoint: the whole card set's distinctive cohesion is the agent's neutralization + house look propagated across every card, not a canned default. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document in a single call; no per-record named file is pulled out.

outputs.name: graded_product_shots_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized product photos delivered as the 1:1 PDP crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, ALONGSIDE their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutral full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralization is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop master of each frame — the in-frame 18% grey card reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point while the house warmth is held, and true-to-product (no product's genuine color forced off); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered 1:1 crop (framed on the product, grey card fully cropped OUT). The neutrality tolerance is NEVER evaluated on the product crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each frame (an applied-settings log, not a measurement).

outputs.name: variant_kettle_burgundy.jpg
outputs.spec: Seasonal-colorway variant of the enamel kettle shot: the bright-red enamel body deepened to a rich seasonal burgundy via a masked, luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl pass pair (a small within-family hue nudge plus a saturation/luminance drop that darkens and mutes the red — an in-band adjacent shift, no near-complementary rotation) riding the enamel's existing luminosity, so its curved-body reflections, sheen highlights and cast shadow stay natural and the counter, linen and beans are untouched — no whole-image overlay, no flat dead-fill.

outputs.name: hero_banner_desktop.jpg
outputs.spec: 1920x720 JPEG, sRGB, web-optimized: the graded product hero (capture_03) reframed to the wide desktop ratio using the source's own generous empty left region as negative space — a pure DOWNSCALE crop of the ~4600 px camera-scale master (no invented or extended pixels), carrying the same house look as the rest of the set.

outputs.name: hero_banner_mobile.jpg
outputs.spec: 1080x1350 JPEG, sRGB, web-optimized: the SAME graded hero master reframed to the tall mobile ratio by cropping the existing frame vertically — a pure downscale crop (no generation), consistent with the desktop banner because both come from one graded master.

outputs.name: cindergrove_mark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the shop wordmark, traced only AFTER the scan (mark_ref_01) is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at header scale with no captured paper ground or skew. This is the mark bound into every PDP card header via @Mark. Its filled counters read correctly on the template's light card ground.

outputs.name: icon_divider_pack
outputs.spec: The storefront icon + section-divider pack, EXPORTED (SVG/PNG) from the client-authored icon_divider_sheet.ai via document_render_vector — single-weight deep-ink strokes, transparent, scalable for the product cards and section breaks. Export only; the connector does not draw these.

outputs.name: decoration_accent.png
outputs.spec: One section-accent graphic: the photographed storefront decal (mark_ref_02) lifted onto a clean transparent ground by image_remove_background and downscaled/reframed to the accent tile — a RASTER cut-out with no vector paths, proving the photographed decal was correctly triaged as a photograph and NOT traced.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: capture_01.jpg, capture_02.jpg, capture_03.jpg, capture_04.jpg, capture_05.jpg, capture_06.jpg, capture_07.jpg, capture_08.jpg, mark_ref_01.png, mark_ref_02.png, icon_divider_sheet.ai
connector_workflow.note: Single asset load: bring the eight product captures, the two shop-mark references and the authored .ai icon sheet into Creative Cloud storage. Every later step consumes a named prior output; this is the only ingest. Plumbing, not difficulty.

Triage: capture_01 is tilted ~+3deg, so level it before neutralizing. (Only the tilted frames 01/05/07 and the scanned mark get straightened; the level frames skip this — deciding which is part of the job.)

Cool shop-fluorescent cast: WARM the temperature and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), then set exposure/highlights/shadows so the card sits at mid-grey. In the SAME call lay the shared AGENT-AUTHORED house look built from primitives — a restrained warm-highlight / cool-neutral-shadow split-tone with modest contrast, a touch of clarity and a gentle, deliberately-not-garish vibrance lift — as batch-wide constants. Reason the exact temperature/exposure to THIS card; do NOT reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. This replaces the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / image_adjust_vibrance_and_saturation and the banned preset/auto_tone 'grade': the look is authored, not picked.

Crop the neutralized frame to the 1:1 1200x1200 the card image frame expects, framing on the dripper with the grey card cropped OUT — this crop is what binds into the card. The pre-crop master c01_neutral (card still in frame) is RETAINED as the neutrality-grading artifact; neutrality is graded THERE, card-exclusion is the separate check on this crop. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand.

Enamel kettle, mixed window+lamp split cast, level: balance temperature AND tint to drive its grey card neutral to the shared white point (a modest, compromise correction since the two sides disagree), plus the shared house-look constants. This neutralized full-res master feeds BOTH the 1:1 PDP crop AND the burgundy recolor branch, so keep it before cropping. Distinct numbers from frame 1. Report the move.
Crop the neutralized kettle to the 1:1 1200x1200 card frame (the bright-red version that binds into the Enamel Kettle card). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Hero, near-neutral light, level: its grey card is close to neutral, so only a SMALL white-balance nudge lands it on the shared white point — over-correcting pushes it off the set. Set exposure to match set brightness, apply the shared house-look constants. This graded wide master feeds BOTH the 1:1 PDP crop AND the two banner reframes, so keep it before cropping. Report the (small) move.
Crop the neutralized hero to the 1:1 1200x1200 card frame, framing on the dripper with the grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

THE TRAP FRAME. The terracotta stoneware is genuinely warm product color and it was shot under near-neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift — only match exposure/brightness to the set and lay the shared house-look constants. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction used on frames 1/2, or that 'cools an imagined blue cast', neutralizes the card off-neutral and strips the terracotta the client is selling. Decision driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was held.
Crop the (WB-held) terracotta frame to the 1:1 1200x1200 card frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted ~+4deg under amber lamp — level it before neutralizing.

Strong amber cast: this frame moves the OPPOSITE direction from the cool frames — COOL it (negative temperature) until its grey card reads neutral and matches the shared white point; hold contrast, apply the shared house-look constants. Adaptive: a blanket 'warm everything' pass fails here. Report the (larger) cooling move.
Crop the neutralized tumbler to the 1:1 1200x1200 card frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Cool north-window, underexposed, level: WARM the temperature and LIFT exposure to the card, protecting the glass specular edge highlights from clipping; apply the shared house-look constants. A tonal problem (lift) distinct from the warm frames. Report the move.
Crop the neutralized carafe to the 1:1 1200x1200 card frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted ~+3deg under green fluorescent — level it before neutralizing.

Green fluorescent cast: neutralize the card with a TINT correction (green to magenta) rather than a temperature move — a DIFFERENT axis from the warm/cool frames; a temperature-only fix leaves the card green and fails the gate. Keep the natural wood tone true, apply the shared house-look constants. Report the tint magnitude.
Crop the neutralized scoop set to the 1:1 1200x1200 card frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Overexposed and warm, level: PULL exposure/highlights DOWN to recover the blown sand, THEN cool to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point — the OPPOSITE tonal AND white-balance direction from the underexposed cool carafe (frame 06), proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. Apply the shared house-look constants. Report the recovery + cooling move. Frames 01-08 now share one white point, each neutralized to its own grey card under the one house look.
Crop the neutralized pour-over stand to the 1:1 1200x1200 card frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

On the graded full-res kettle master, semantically select only the red enamel kettle body ('the red enamel kettle body'). Isolates the recolor to the object so the counter, linen and beans are untouched. Returns a maskURI. Not a hue/coordinate selection — a real object.

Masked recolor pass 1 (consumes kettle master + mask): keep the enamel in the red family but deepen it toward burgundy — a small within-band hue nudge (well under ~60deg, staying in red/wine; NOT a near-complementary rotation) together with a luminance drop that darkens the enamel, letting its existing luminosity carry the curved-body reflections, sheen highlights and cast shadow. Confined to the mask. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would tint the whole scene) and image_fill_area is flat solid dead-fill (kills the enamel sheen) — both are wrong here.

Masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): trim the red-band saturation and settle the luminance so the enamel lands on the rich seasonal burgundy target instead of a flat brick or a still-bright candy red, still riding the original luminosity so the sheen and shadow stay natural. A deepen-and-mute in the same hue family, not a swing to a new hue.

Resize the finished burgundy kettle variant to the same 1:1 web frame as the set. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. A standalone seasonal-colorway deliverable (the standard red kettle still binds into the merge via c02_pdp).

Reframe the graded wide hero master to the 1920x720 desktop banner, using its generous empty left region as the negative space — a pure DOWNSCALE crop of the ~4600 px master (edges cropped away to hit the wide ratio, no invented pixels). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand.

Reframe the SAME graded hero master to the 1080x1350 mobile banner by cropping the existing frame vertically — a pure downscale crop, consistent with the desktop banner because both come from one graded master. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

MARK BRANCH — the flat scanned wordmark (the traceable source). Prep-before-trace step 1: the scan sits ~2deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the off-white paper toward white so the espresso lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges. (image_apply_adjustments, replacing any deprecated brightness/contrast tool.)
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). The enclosed counters fill with the crisped-to-white ground and read correctly on the template's LIGHT card header.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the card header. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. This SVG binds into every card via @Mark.

TRIAGE BRANCH — the CORRECT treatment for the photographed decal. mark_ref_02 is a PHOTOGRAPH of a painted decal on a textured plaster wall, so it is NOT traced; instead knock the wall to transparency, isolating the decal as a clean cut-out. Feeding this file to image_vectorize (as the scanned wordmark was) would produce garbage plaster-weave/perspective paths — that is the invisible triage failure the agent must avoid.
Downscale/reframe the decal cut-out to the section-accent tile — a raster cut-out with no vector paths, from the 2600x2600 source (downscale-only, never upscale). onSubjectClipping='extract'.
Export the client-authored .ai icon/divider library to SVG/PNG (export only — does not draw the icons). This is the storefront icon/divider pack deliverable.

chaining_note: Strict output->input chaining throughout; the single ingest at step 1 (uploaded_assets) is the only load, and every later step consumes a named prior output. BATCH BRANCH: eight per-photo grade sub-chains fan out from uploaded_assets, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization to that frame's own in-frame grey card (adaptive: warm the cool fluorescent frame 01, compromise-balance the split-cast kettle 02, small-nudge the near-neutral hero 03, HOLD WB on the genuinely-terracotta frame 04, cool the amber frame 05, warm+lift the underexposed cool carafe 06, tint-correct the green frame 07, recover+cool the overexposed frame 08) carrying one shared agent-authored house look as constants, each followed by a 1:1 1200x1200 crop, with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames 01/05/07 — every neutralization converges on one shared white point. RECOLOR BRANCH: the kettle's neutralized full-res master c02_neutral (step 5) feeds image_select_by_prompt(21) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(22) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(23) -> resize(24), the two HSL passes both consuming kettle_mask. BANNER BRANCH: the hero's neutralized wide master c03_neutral (step 7) forks into two downscale reframes, 1920x720 desktop(25) and 1080x1350 mobile(26). MARK BRANCH: mark_ref_01 runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain — straighten(27) -> crisp adjustments(28) -> crop_to_bounds(29) -> remove_background to transparency(30) -> vectorize(31) = cindergrove_mark.svg. TRIAGE BRANCH: mark_ref_02 (a photograph) is routed AWAY from the tracer to remove_background(32) -> reframe(33) = decoration_accent.png. The authored .ai exports via document_render_vector(34). The eight graded photos and the mark SVG converge into the upload session(35) -> finalize(36) -> document_merge_data_layout(37), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the roster CSV and emits one merged card per row, resolving BOTH the @Product column (that row's graded photo) and the @Mark column (the shared vectorized mark, identical in every row) into the template's two merge-wired image frames — the only connector-doable path for the mark since free-form placement is banned. The merged set is exported once by document_render_layout(38) to the single press-ready PDF carrying all eight cards (one page per SKU); no per-record named export is attempted. graded_product_shots_x8 is the eight 1:1 crops plus their RETAINED neutralized masters; the params report logs the per-frame corrective moves.
difficulty_rationale: Depth, not plumbing or breadth: 38 connector calls across 14 distinct Adobe tools spanning four groups (raster grading/masking/vectorize, asset storage, vector export, document merge/export), well above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the single asset_add_file ingest and the two upload steps. The core is NOT a repeated recipe: each of the eight neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision (cool fluorescent warmed, split cast compromise-balanced, near-neutral hero small-nudged, genuinely-terracotta frame HELD, amber cooled, underexposed cool carafe warmed+lifted, green tint-corrected, overexposed frame recovered+cooled) on differing axes (temperature vs green/magenta tint vs tonal lift/recovery), all forced to converge on one measurable target — the in-frame 18% grey card — so a blanket batch correction cannot pass. Layered on top: an agent-authored house look built from image_apply_adjustments primitives (split-tone + contrast/clarity/restrained vibrance) applied as shared constants (NOT a preset, NOT auto_tone); a masked luminosity-preserving within-family bright-red -> burgundy recolor executed as two image_adjust_hsl passes with a written rationale for why color_overlay and fill_area are both wrong; a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white scan; a triage routing a photographed decal AWAY from the tracer to remove_background; two honest downscale banner reframes from a camera-scale master; and a two-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template (the row's graded photo via @Product and the shared vectorized mark via @Mark). Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand/inpaint, no text-to-image, no compositing, no upscaling, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used; image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _vibrance_and_saturation / _brightness_and_contrast are replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): every product photo carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and the acceptance criterion is that each frame's card, graded on its RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master (grey card still present), reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a hair of zero) with the whole set matched to one white point and the house warmth held — a target the agent can miss by choosing the wrong per-frame move, and it must REPORT the final white-balance and exposure move per frame so 'matched' is verifiable rather than asserted; card-exclusion is a SEPARATE gate checked on the 1:1 product crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the cards, so the neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop; the merge adds a third checkable gate (output page-count must equal roster row-count = 8, since document_merge_data_layout is one-file-per-row). HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset neutralization of eight differently-lit product shots to a common measurable white point, each needing its own opposite-direction correction on differing axes (temperature vs green/magenta tint vs exposure recovery), which a novice cannot match by eye; (2) a masked, luminosity-preserving bright-red -> burgundy seasonal recolor (a within-family deepen-and-mute) that must keep enamel sheen and shadow natural using the only masked recolor path (image_adjust_hsl), not color_overlay (whole-image) or fill_area (flat dead-fill); (3) prep-before-trace discipline on a skewed, off-white, margin-padded wordmark scan (straighten->crisp->crop-to-bounds->knock-to-transparency) before vectorize. TRAP: the terracotta stoneware (capture_04) is genuinely warm and was shot under neutral light, so its grey card is already neutral — the naive path batch-applies the same 'warm the cool cast' correction used on the fluorescent frames (or 'cools an imagined blue cast'), which pushes its card off-neutral and strips the real product color; the correct path reads THAT card and holds white balance. A second trap sits in the mark triage: mark_ref_02 looks like 'a second logo capture' but is a PHOTOGRAPH of a decal on a textured wall — running it through the prep-and-vectorize path used on the scanned wordmark yields garbage paths, a failure invisible until the SVG is opened; the correct route is remove_background for the accent. A third trap sits in the merge: attempting a multi-product grid card, or feeding a convert_pdf_to_indd template, both fail to bind/produce; only the supplied single-record authored .indd merges correctly. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (stated as decoupled claims so no artifact is graded on a region it crops away): (a) grey card neutral (channel spread near zero) and one shared white point with the house warmth held, evaluated on all eight RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (card still in frame), never on a card-removed crop; (b) card-exclusion checked separately on the eight 1:1 crops that bind into the cards; plus the agent reports per-frame WB/exposure params, the kettle recolored within its mask only, the wordmark a clean skew-free transparent-ground vector, the two banners at exactly 1920x720 and 1080x1350 from real cropped pixels, and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI card per roster row.
